messages:
zoe_sales: Hi team — Tasha from HelixCare wants to confirm connectivity for their Private deployment. Their environment is split across two AWS accounts (svc-account and corp-account). Requirements: 1) end-to-end mTLS so Helix's services validate client certs all the way to the app; 2) original client IP in app logs for their SIEM; 3) they prefer not to stand up VPN/DX. Can we support this using PrivateLink cross-account? Any pricing notes?

alan_neteng: Short: cross-account PrivateLink is supported, but notable limitations re: L3 client IP visibility and pure TCP passthrough for mTLS. Explanation: PrivateLink (interface endpoint) in the consumer account connects to a Network Load Balancer (NLB) in the provider account. The NLB->target chain can be configured to preserve source IPs if you use IP targets and operate at L4. However, when we terminate TLS at an ingress proxy (L7) we can inject X-Forwarded-For. If Helix needs mutual TLS validated by the actual backend app (not a proxy), we need TLS passthrough to the backend targets — that can be achieved by keeping the NLB in TCP mode and not terminating TLS at the ALB/proxy layer.

vikram_sre: Adding detail: two practical patterns:
- Pattern A (PrivateLink + TCP passthrough): Provider exposes an NLB (TCP) with TLS passthrough. Interface endpoint connects to that NLB. Backend instances must handle mTLS (client cert validation). This preserves client source IPs to the extent NLB preserves them (enable `preserve client ip` via target type=ip and proxy protocol off). Caveat: AWS sometimes shows ENI addresses in flow logs; upstream app should read the real socket source. We should validate with a small test.
- Pattern B (PrivateLink + ingress proxy): terminate TLS at a managed proxy (we control), validate client certs at proxy, then mutual auth between proxy and app can be mTLS or internal TLS. Proxy adds `X-Forwarded-For` for original IP. This is easier operationally but shifts the cert verification boundary to our proxy.

tasha_cust: If we go with Pattern A (passthrough), do you support OCSP/CRL checks at the app level? Also, will there be extra per-ENI or per-endpoint charges we should expect?

alan_neteng: OCSP/CRL would be handled by the app (or a sidecar) in Pattern A. For Pattern B we can perform OCSP/CRL at our proxy and report. Pricing: PrivateLink interface endpoints have AWS charges on the consumer side+data processing; on Redwood side we charge the standard Private deployment rate. If we need to run dedicated NLB capacity and reserve IP target instances in a dedicated account (for cross-account routing simplicity), that can add a moderate infra premium (monthly). If they avoid VPN/DX, costs are usually lower but the one-time integration/testing fee may still apply. I'll ask finance for a ballpark delta.

acct-bot: Note: typical add-on pricing for "dedicated cross-account NLB support" historically ~ +15% monthly infra for medium workloads; "managed TLS passthrough testing" is a one-time services fee. (Estimate only)

vikram_sre: Also: if Helix needs the raw source IP in application logs and they use PrivateLink, we must confirm the NIC+kernel semantics on our targets. For IP target mode NLBs we usually see the client's private IP on the socket; for instance target mode it's the ENI IP. Recommend a two-hour validation test during POC to prove the behavior.

tasha_cust: That test sounds good. We also need to ensure cert rotation can be automated and that our security team can revoke certs quickly — must support OCSP/CRL and an API for revocation events.

alan_neteng: We support automated rotation for server certs. For client cert revocation, two options: 1) App-level OCSP/CRL (you run your OCSP responder and our backend can reach it if using Pattern A and network routes permit). 2) If Pattern B, our proxy can perform OCSP/CRL checks and we can integrate with your revocation API (webhook) for near-real-time revocation. We'll document SLA for revocation propagation.

zoe_sales: Action items: 1) Alan: draft simple architecture diagrams for Pattern A and B + recommended config flags (NLB target type=ip, TLS:pass-through), 2) Vikram: schedule two-hour validation window and test plan, 3) Finance: provide ballpark delta for dedicated NLB/reserved infra + one-time integration fee, 4) Tasha: confirm POC test window availability.

infra-bot: New test environment provisioned: redwood-poc-helix-2026-04 (uploader: infra-bot).

alan_neteng: Example text for the Helix security questionnaire (feel free to copy):
```
Q: Can you support end-to-end mTLS with original client IPs preserved via PrivateLink?
A: Yes. Two supported patterns:
  - Pattern A (TLS passthrough): PrivateLink -> NLB (TCP) -> backend instances. Configure NLB target type=ip for client source preservation; backend validates client certs and OCSP/CRL. We recommend a short validation test during POC to confirm socket-level source IP semantics.
  - Pattern B (TLS termination at ingress proxy): PrivateLink -> ingress proxy (Redwood terminates mTLS, performs OCSP/CRL checks) -> internal mTLS/tls to backend. Proxy injects `X-Forwarded-For` with original IPs.
Note: PrivateLink interface endpoint charges and AWS data-processing fees apply on the consumer side. Additional Redwood infra reserved capacity for dedicated NLBs or cross-account facilitation may incur a monthly premium and a one-time integration fee.
```

vikram_sre: I'll post the test plan in the shared folder and tag you, Tasha. We should include a curl/openssl snippet to prove client IPs and cert validation.

tasha_cust: Great, available Wednesday afternoon for the POC. If pricing looks reasonable we'll move to finalize SOW next week.

zoe_sales: Perfect. I'll update the deal card and add the POC milestone. Thanks all :rocket:
